contextual.summary: Manchester reviews every UCAS application automatically for WP, WP Plus and WP Plus PLUS flags; flagged applicants whose course needs ABB or higher can get a contextual offer one or two grades lower, and care-experienced and refugee applicants have their own lower offer.
contextual.typicalReduction: WP Plus: usually one grade lower than the standard offer; WP Plus PLUS: usually two grades lower

criteria.detail: Home postcode in ACORN category 5 (Stretched Society) or 6 (Low Income Living). The postcode alone gives a WP flag, not a contextual offer.
Home postcode in TUNDRA quintile 1 (higher education participation). The postcode alone gives a WP flag, not a contextual offer.
Home postcode in IMD quintile 1 (disadvantage). The postcode alone gives a WP flag, not a contextual offer.
GCSE or A-level school/college performed below the national average (averaged over up to three years); together with the postcode criteria this gives a WP Plus flag.
Eligible for free school meals during secondary education (England, Northern Ireland, Wales; checked from official data, not self-declared); gives a WP Plus flag.
In care in the UK for more than three months; gives a WP Plus PLUS flag.
Permission to stay in the UK as a refugee, asylum seeker, under humanitarian protection or on a Ukraine scheme; gives a WP Plus PLUS flag.
Young adult carer (under 25 on 1 September of the year of entry, UK resident); gives a WP Plus PLUS flag.

Completed the Manchester Access Programme (Year 12, Greater Manchester): reduced offer of up to two grades. The Arthur Lewis Assignment gives Social Sciences offer-holders a one-grade reduction and the Manchester Distance Access Scheme gives eligible offer-holders on some other courses a one-grade reduction.

contextual.rulesText: WP flag = home postcode meets the ACORN, TUNDRA or IMD criteria. WP Plus flag = postcode criteria plus a below-average school, or free school meals. WP Plus PLUS flag = refugee/asylum/humanitarian protection/Ukraine scheme, care for more than three months, or young adult carer. Contextual offers only apply to WP Plus or WP Plus PLUS applicants whose course has standard entry requirements of ABB or higher and who meet the published entry requirements. Applicants are assessed automatically from their UCAS form; the postcode and school checks are for UK applicants under 21 only.

source.evidence: If you meet our WP Plus criteria, the contextual offer is usually one grade lower than the standard entry requirements.

flagsSource.evidence: You’ll be assigned a WP flag if your home postcode meets our criteria (Acorn category 5 or 6, TUNDRA Quintile 1 or IMD Quintile 1).

programmes.name: Manchester Access Programme (MAP)
programmes.summary: A skills-based programme for local Year 12 students (online and on-campus events, workshops and a 1,500-word academic essay) that earns a reduced Manchester offer.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students who live in Greater Manchester or study at a school or college there, attend a state post-16 school or college on a two-year Level 3 course, have at least five GCSEs at grade 6 or above (and at least a 4 in English Language and Maths) and meet at least one priority criterion such as free school meals, first generation, care experience, estrangement, refugee/asylum seeker status or being a young carer.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Essential: live in Greater Manchester or study at a school or college there; Year 12; at least five GCSEs at grade 6+ with at least grade 4 in English Language and Maths; only non-fee-paying schools attended; state post-16 school or college studying a two-year Level 3 qualification equivalent to three A-levels; home-registered or settled student. Plus at least one Category A priority criterion (free school meals or pupil premium, no parent/carer with a degree, local authority care experience for any length of time, estranged, sanctuary seeker, young carer). Category B criteria (low-progression area, below-average school, disability, military family, some ethnic groups, discretionary 16-19 bursary) only count alongside a Category A criterion.
benefits: Reduced offer of up to two A-level grades at Manchester
Undergraduate Access Scholarship currently worth £1,300 per year if you study at Manchester
Early decision on your application before you apply through UCAS
Travel costs to interviews and visit days paid for students who complete MAP
programmes.subjects: All subjects (separate Medicine and Dentistry strands)

runs.text: April to August 2027: Start your Journey event in April, academic module from May, open day visit in June, final event in July, essay submitted in August (about 50 hours in total)

programmes.infoNote: Details are for MAP 2027 (applications are open now); the eligibility criteria may change for MAP 2028.

programmes.provider: The University of Manchester (School of Social Sciences)
programmes.summary: A distance-learning pre-university course for Social Sciences offer-holders (including Economics) that earns a one-grade reduction to the standard entry requirements on successful completion.
programmes.whoCanApply: Offer-holders for a School of Social Sciences undergraduate course whose application has a WP flag (low-progression or deprived neighbourhood) and/or a WP Plus flag (in or has been in local authority care for more than three months).
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Hold an offer for a School of Social Sciences undergraduate course; live in a neighbourhood with a low progression rate to higher education or high deprivation (WP flag) and/or be living in, or have lived in, local authority care for more than three months (WP Plus flag). Eligible students are emailed from February.
benefits: One-grade reduction to the standard entry requirements on a Social Sciences course on successful completion (BSc Economics offer-holders need an A in Mathematics)

programmes.name: Manchester Distance Access Scheme (MDAS)
programmes.summary: An online pre-university scheme for offer-holders (an Academic Skills Module and a Mini Degree Module) that earns an offer one A-level grade lower on eligible courses, including International Business, Finance and Economics.
programmes.whoCanApply: Offer-holders from the UK who are under 21, study at a UK education provider, live in an area with low progression to higher education or a less advantaged neighbourhood, have not attended an independent or fee-paying school, and make Manchester their firm choice.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Hold an offer from Manchester and choose it as your firm choice; be a permanent UK resident and under 21; study at a UK education provider; live in an area with low progression to higher education or a less advantaged neighbourhood; not have attended an independent or fee-paying school; not already hold a higher education qualification; not be taking an Access to Higher Education qualification; not have completed the Manchester Access Programme. The School of Social Sciences runs its own scheme (the Arthur Lewis Assignment) instead.
benefits: An offer one A-level grade below the standard offer (for example AAA becomes AAB)
University-level teaching before starting your course
Can be added to a contextual offer for WP Plus applicants (for example standard AAA becomes ABB)
